source: cheat the game cheat you run around a park and if you get caught buy the taga when you are on the ground you in when the timer runs out the player that is in gets eliminated and its last man standing

answers.ask: No look was given - should the park read as bright and stylised, or an ordinary modern city park?
answers.answer: Make it a bright, stylised park so the tag game is easy to read and playful.

answers.ask: How big should the park be - one open field you can cross in a few seconds, or a whole park with several areas?
answers.answer: Use one small open park field that players can cross in a few seconds; keep the first build simple and focused.

answers.ask: Where do eliminated players go while the round finishes?
answers.answer: Eliminated players should go to a simple spectator area above or beside the park and watch until the round ends.

## Clarifications resolved
- [author] theme — Q: No look was given - should the park read as bright and stylised, or an ordinary modern city park? A: Make it a bright, stylised park so the tag game is easy to read and playful.
- [author] scale — Q: How big should the park be - one open field you can cross in a few seconds, or a whole park with several areas? A: Use one small open park field that players can cross in a few seconds; keep the first build simple and focused.
- [author] goal — Q: Where do eliminated players go while the round finishes? A: Eliminated players should go to a simple spectator area above or beside the park and watch until the round ends.
- [agent_inferred] spectator_position — Q: Should the spectator area be elevated or beside the field? A: Put it beside the field at ground level, separated from play, to keep the first build simple.

## Enriched image prompt
Create a small, bright, stylised park tag arena built around one open grassy field that players can cross in a few seconds. Keep the running space simple, continuous, and easy to read, with a clear perimeter and evenly distributed start positions around the field. Place a compact spectator area beside the park at ground level, physically separated from active play but facing the whole field so eliminated players can watch the round.

## Genre
The genre is Party & Casual, canonical slug `party-casual`, because this is a round-based childhood tag game with last-player-standing elimination.

## Shape and preset
Use `space-bounded`, the Party & Casual-specific SocialZone (Continuous Play Space), because the park field itself is the entire match space. The matched preset is Childhood Game, with its maze and dense hide-and-seek clutter omitted because the author confirmed one simple open field.

## Config requirements
Use `spectator-zone` for the small ground-level viewing area beside the park, separated from play and oriented toward the field. No maze, dense cover array, separate lobby, or other image option is grounded in the confirmed simple build.

## Layout requirements
Place `spawn-protected` SpawnZones evenly around the open park field so no player begins with an unfair positional advantage. Place `trigger-scoring` TriggerZones as the tag-detection regions required by the round, tied to the active play field rather than the spectator area. Keep the spectator area outside every active-play trigger.

## Layout components
The build contains one small open grassy park field, one clear outer perimeter, evenly distributed round-start positions, and one compact ground-level spectator area beside the field with an unobstructed view across it. The spectator divider forms the only internal boundary. Compose the whole field and spectator area together in one readable frame.

## Render order
Use `isometric`: render the playful field and adjacent spectator composition first, then derive the uncomplicated top-down plan. The isometric image is authoritative because no generated maze, racing route, or other topology needs computation.

## Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
The scale is small, driven by the confirmed field that can be crossed in a few seconds. The theme is a bright, playful, stylised park. Use `P0`; the park and ground-level spectator area share one simple surface with no overhang, interior transition, separate map, or validity-by-construction requirement.
